findings.description: Browsers get no instruction against framing, MIME sniffing or script injection.

findings.evidence: Server: Apache/2.4.29 (Ubuntu) PHP/7.2.24; X-Powered-By: PHP/7.2.24 WooCommerce/3.5.1
findings.description: The stack and its versions are announced to anyone.

findings.evidence: the query is echoed unescaped inside <h1>

findings.evidence: POST /cart with price=1 gives a 1 € line for a 120 € product
findings.description: The price is read from the form instead of the catalogue.

findings.evidence: form with fields card, exp, cvv posted to http://
findings.description: Card numbers travel in clear and are handled by the shop itself.

findings.evidence: order 1002 (name, e-mail, address, card ending) returned without any session
findings.description: Any order is readable by changing the number.

findings.evidence: error text differs for a valid username; 50 attempts in 10 s accepted
findings.description: Usernames can be enumerated and passwords brute-forced.

findings.evidence: Set-Cookie: session=admin-7c9e; Path=/ (no HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite)
findings.description: The session cookie can be read by script and sent cross-site.

findings.evidence: request with Cookie: session=admin-7c9e returns the admin dashboard
findings.description: The session value is static and guessable.
The file points attackers to the sensitive paths.

findings.evidence: DB_PASSWORD, SMTP_PASSWORD and STRIPE_SECRET returned with HTTP 200
findings.description: Database, mail and payment secrets are public.
Configuration and database backups are downloadable.

findings.evidence: names, e-mails and phone numbers returned without authentication
findings.description: Customer personal data is public: a GDPR breach.
